candidate.analysis: The program reads /input/public_csv, validates the expected columns, computes fish-per-hour outcomes, summarizes central tendency and variability, compares rates by livebait and camper status, reports Pearson correlations with numeric predictors, and fits a simple ordinary least-squares model for fish caught using hours, livebait, camper, persons, and child. It prints concise observations only.
candidate.answer: Visitors caught an average of 1.107 fish per hour (median 0). Live bait was associated with higher rates (1.220 vs 0.390), and campers likewise (1.347 vs 0.765). Persons showed the strongest positive rate correlation (0.218); hours (-0.068), livebait (0.064), camper (0.065), and children (-0.029) were weakly correlated. In the OLS model, hours, livebait, camper, and persons had positive coefficients, while child had a negative coefficient.
